# Anthropic IPO Priced at $83 Per Share in Largest-Ever Tech Debut


By OpenTools Team


·


November 19, 2026


Anthropic priced its blockbuster IPO at $83 per share late Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion and valuing the Claude maker at roughly $1.5 trillion. Trading begins Thursday on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, making it the largest public market debut in history — and a referendum on whether Wall Street still believes in the AI boom.


## The Numbers: $81.3 Billion Raised at $83 Per Share


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) priced its long-awaited initial public offering at **$83 per share** late Wednesday, selling 980 million shares and raising $81.3 billion, according to[Investor's Business Daily](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/anthropic-ipo-pricing-debut-ai-stocks/) . The price came in above the company's previously stated range of $70 to $78, signaling stronger-than-expected demand from institutional investors.


The 980 million shares included 801.4 million from Anthropic itself and 23.6 million sold by co-founders. Underwriters have the option to purchase an additional 123.75 million shares, which could push total proceeds to roughly $91.6 billion. Alongside the public offering,[IBD](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/anthropic-ipo-pricing-debut-ai-stocks/) reports Anthropic also planned a $26 billion private placement.


The IPO values Anthropic at approximately **$1.5 trillion** on a fully diluted basis, placing it among the world's most valuable public companies overnight. For context, SpaceX raised $75 billion in its June IPO — a figure that now looks modest by comparison.


- **Share price** $83 (above the $70-$78 expected range)


- **Shares sold** 980 million (including 23.6M from co-founders)


- **Total raised** $81.3 billion (up to $91.6B with overallotment)


- **Private placement** $26 billion alongside the public offering


- **Market valuation** ~$1.5 trillion fully diluted


- **Ticker** ANT on Nasdaq, trading starts Thursday Nov 19


## The First Frontier AI Lab Tests Public Markets


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is the first so-called frontier AI lab — companies building the most advanced, general-purpose AI models — to go public. Founded in 2021 by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, both former[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) employees, Anthropic has positioned itself as the safety-conscious alternative in the AI race while simultaneously building what many consider the best-performing models available.


While not the $2 trillion figure that Anthropic was reportedly discussing in earlier talks with investors, the $1.5 trillion valuation still makes this the largest tech IPO in history.[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/anthropic-ipo-valuation-ai-boom-rcna610069) notes that Anthropic's public arrival will serve as "more than just a measure of what Wall Street thinks the company is worth — it will be a test of current sentiment around AI itself at a pivotal moment for the industry."


[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/18/anthropic-share-price-stock-market-ipo) reports that co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei will ring the opening bell at the Nasdaq exchange when shares begin trading Thursday morning.


## Claude's Track Record: Fable and Claude Code


The investor enthusiasm is backed by real product momentum. Claude's latest edition, codenamed **Fable** , ranks No. 1 on Artificial Analysis' leaderboard of top-performing large language models, capable of handling complex computer engineering tasks that rival and often surpass offerings from[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) and[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) .


But the real growth driver has been **Claude Code** ,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's agentic coding tool. Released in February 2025, it became what[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/anthropic-ipo-valuation-ai-boom-rcna610069) noted is "the fastest-growing product in enterprise software history," hitting $1 billion in revenue within six months of launch. The tool is now used throughout the tech industry for autonomous code generation, debugging, and multi-file refactoring.


Thursday's IPO is expected to mint a new crop of billionaires and multi-millionaires as Anthropic's seven co-founders and early employees see their equity converted into publicly traded shares.


## A Referendum on AI at a Fragile Moment


The IPO lands at a precarious time for the AI industry. The tech-heavy Nasdaq, which was up 19% for the year as recently as a few weeks ago, had risen by less than 5% as of Wednesday,[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/anthropic-ipo-valuation-ai-boom-rcna610069) reports. AI skepticism has been mounting on multiple fronts: public opposition to data center construction, Democrats winning control of Congress on an AI-skeptical platform, and growing concern about the sustainability of infrastructure spending.


James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, told[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/anthropic-ipo-valuation-ai-boom-rcna610069) : "Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom."


"With the selloff in technology stocks continuing this week," McCann added, "investors will be watching to see how well the[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) IPO is received."


> "Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom."


**James McCann** - Senior Economist, Edward Jones


## Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit Casts a Shadow


Compounding the uncertainty: the **resignation of Jensen Huang** from[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) . The chip giant has been the financial backbone of the AI economy, both as a hardware supplier and as an investor in smaller AI firms. His departure, reported by[Investor's Business Daily](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/anthropic-ipo-pricing-debut-ai-stocks/) , has sent ripples through the sector, with Nvidia stock falling and broader AI stocks under pressure.


McCann told[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/anthropic-ipo-valuation-ai-boom-rcna610069) : "The leadership change at Nvidia adds to short-term uncertainty around the sector, particularly given the important role this giant company has played in financially supporting a range of smaller technology firms in recent years."


Some analysts see the IPO as a potential circuit-breaker. According to[Investor's Business Daily](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/anthropic-ipo-pricing-debut-ai-stocks/) , one analyst called[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's debut a "big near-term win" for an AI rally in need of a kick-start. A strong first day of trading could restore confidence; a weak one could deepen the selloff.


## What Changes for Builders Using Claude


For the developers and teams that rely on Claude Code daily,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's public listing introduces both opportunities and questions. As a public company, Anthropic will face quarterly earnings pressure — which typically means more aggressive pricing strategies, faster product iteration, and potentially broader enterprise feature rollouts to justify the valuation.


The $26 billion private placement alongside the IPO gives Anthropic a substantial war chest for model training and infrastructure. Builders can expect continued investment in Claude's capabilities, particularly in coding and agentic workflows where the product already leads. However, public company dynamics also tend to accelerate monetization — API pricing changes and enterprise-tier gating are worth watching closely in the quarters ahead.


The IPO also makes Anthropic's financials public for the first time, giving builders transparency into the company's revenue, costs, and customer concentration that was previously unavailable. That data, expected in the first quarterly filing, will reveal just how dependent Anthropic's business is on enterprise contracts versus individual developer usage.


- **More investment** $26B private placement funds continued model training and infrastructure


- **Pricing pressure** Public company dynamics may accelerate API monetization and enterprise-tier changes


- **Financial transparency** First quarterly filing will reveal revenue breakdowns and customer concentration


- **Product velocity** Quarterly earnings pressure typically drives faster feature shipping
